After a trio of hit EPs including last fall's "While I Stay Secluded," the band signed with Rise Records to release their first full-length. The album's title comes from the idea that even though the lyrics to the songs are about being hurt and upset, at the end of the day everything is fine and everything is copacetic (Nick Casasanto). Knuckle Puck will be playing all summer long on the Vans Warped Tour.

The Choosing is the name of the spawn obstacle course that will determine if a player is "worthy" the server. I say this lightly couse I don't want this to be a punishment, but rather an enjoyful experience that might make you feel more related to server in the end.

The goal of The Choosing is to challenge the player's psyche and physique (in-game) in ways that is required to be fit for the server. Through puzzles, parkour courses, choices, quizzes, labyrinths. Please come with suggestions.

One thing to keep in mind is the difficulty to create puzzles and obstacles that more people can do at the same time.

 

Here's list of the challenges we have till now:

-- Parkour course
This is the first challenge new players will face. This is a test to challenge your keyboard and mouse skills. And also they are fun.

-- Labyrinth
A test to challenge your memory and orientation skills. Timed labyrinth?

-- Public duel
Fit to be one of the last challenges. Face another initiate in a public arena. The winner joins the server. Existing members of the server can come and watch.

-- Decorate and make the existing structures more aesthetically pleasing. Both interior and exterior. Currently I've just made something fast to act as an outline
-- Create the parkour course in the 1st level of the The choosing tower.

There has been a surprising amount of literature on this question. Philosophers seem to lean towards yes. Ex-PA governor Ed Rendell says yes. While Rendell may not be the best politician, he knows a thing or two about hot dogs, because he had a hot dog named after him in Harrisburg. USA Today, ESPN, and Gawker all say that a hot dog is a sandwich. The chowhound online community had a lengthy debate on the subject, and women on Reddit seem to hold very passionate views on the subject (don't worry, I used archive.org to link to archives of the Gawker and Reddit pages).

Personally, I tend to agree with John Hodgman. A hot dog is not a sandwich because, as the philosopher Dr. Calvin Normore has noted, hot dogs were invented long before we invented sandwiches. Also, if I asked you for a sandwich and you gave me a hot dog I would be surprised, because when I ask for a sandwich I don't intend to be asking for a hot dog. Finally, the hot dog sandwich exists because hot dogs, in and of themselves, are not sandwiches, unless you slice them and put them between two pieces of sliced bread rather than in a bun like some kind of barbarian.
